ky_great_wall_the.blurb: A mostly sport sandstone wall within Muir Valley in the Red River Gorge, set near the Hideout and reached along the valley-floor trail system. Sixteen climbs, fourteen of them bolted and two on gear. The grades start at easy 5.6 and top out around 5.12, but the bulk of the lines sit in the 5.11 range, with a handful of 5.9s and 5.10s for warming up. Lines run shorter than at its bigger neighbour, yet the stone is rated as high quality, so it suits a mixed group wanting a day with a moderate-to-hard spread rather than a long wall of single-grade climbing.

ky_solar_collector.blurb: An east-facing sandstone wall in Coal Bank Hollow, on the Pendergrass-Murray preserve side of the Red River Gorge. Of its sixteen climbs, fourteen are sport and two are trad. This is a harder-leaning crag: most lines fall in the 5.11 and 5.12 range, with one 5.13 and only a couple of easier outings in the 5.8 to 5.10 zone. The cliff grows taller toward its right end, so the longest lines are there. Holds are on the small side for the Red, with some huecos in the rock, and the tops of routes can stay damp after rain.
